title: Protocol to package and concentrate adeno-associated virus serotype 8 for use in autochthonous mouse models of pancreatic cancer
protocol: Plate 3.5 × 10^7 293T cells in a 15 cm plate in DMEM containing 10% FBS (without antibiotics).
Check 293T cell state by microscope the next day.
Warm DMEM and 1 mg/mL PEI-MAX at room temperature for 30 min if cells have reached 80%–90% confluency.
Prepare a plasmid mixture in a 15 mL tube with 22 μg pHelper, 14.3 μg pAAV8.RepCap, and 13.7 μg pAAV_sgGOI_sg3TSG_Cre in pure DMEM to give a final volume of 2 mL.
Vortex the plasmid mixture for 15 s and centrifuge briefly.
Add 0.15 mL of 1 mg/mL PEI Max to 0.85 mL pure DMEM for a final volume of 1 mL (a ratio of 3 μg PEI Max to 1 μg DNA).
Mix the PEI-MAX solution well by vortexing for 15 s and centrifuge briefly.
Place both 15 mL tubes at room temperature for 5 min.
Add PEI-MAX to the plasmid mixture and pipette up and down several times.
Incubate the transfection mixture at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Slowly drop the transfection mixture into the dish containing 293T cells.
Gently rock the cell plates to mix well.
Add 50 μg of total DNA per 15 cm plate, maintaining a molar ratio of 1:1:1 among the three plasmids.
Replace the DNA-containing transfection media with prewarmed complete DMEM media containing serum and antibiotics after 12-16 hours post-transfection.
Prewarm the complete DMEM media for 30 minutes at 37°C before replacing it.
Gently add the fresh media to avoid disturbing the transfected 293T cells.
Culture the cells for another 48 hours.
Harvest AAV8– Day 3 Timing: 1.5–2.5 h Around 72 h after transfection, the AAV is harvested.
Transfer the supernatant into a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 800 × g for 10 min at 4°C.
Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 μm syringe filter into a new 50 mL tube.
Store the filtered supernatant at 4°C.
Harvest the cells from the 15 cm plate by adding 5 mL lysis buffer per plate.
Gently pipette the transfected 293T cells and collect the cell suspension in a 15 mL tube.
Place the 15 mL tube of cell lysate in −20°C freezer for 10 min (freeze).
Thaw the tube in a 37°C water bath for another 10 min.
Repeat the freeze/thaw cycle two more times.
Spin down the cell lysate at 3,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant of the cell lysate into a 50 mL tube containing filtered culture media.
Add 1 volume of concentrator to 3 volumes of the supernatant mixture.
Firmly close the lid of the 50 mL tube and incubate with constant rocking at around 60 RPM for at least 12 hours in a 4°C freezer.
Gently pipette up and down several times or vortex briefly (5 seconds) between each freeze and thaw reaction.
The next day, spin down the mixture in the 50 mL tube at 1,600 × g for 60 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant using an electric suction apparatus without disturbing the pellet.
Thoroughly resuspend the viral pellet into 600–1,000 μL of recovery solution.
Transfer the resuspended material into a new low-binding 1.5 mL EP tube.
Incubate with constant rocking at around 60 RPM for at least 4 hours at 4°C.
Centrifuge for 3 minutes at 13,000 × g and 4°C to remove cellular and protein debris.
Transfer the clarified supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Aliquot AAV8 at 25–50 μL and store at −80°C until use.
Avoid repeated freeze-thaw cycles of AAV8.
Addition of 0.001% Pluronic F68 can prevent AAV8 aggregation during storage in the freezer.
Prepare a standard curve: Prepare pAAV_sgGOI_sg3TSG_Cre plasmid solution at 10 ng/μL to generate a standard curve.
Make 7 serial dilutions, in duplicate, of your standard curve plasmid.
Dilute one aliquot of AAV8 from −80°C by mixing 2 μl of AAV8 with 198 μL ddH2O (100-fold).
Pipette up and down for several times to ensure thorough dilution.
Dilute 10 μL of this first dilution into 190 μL ddH2O to make a 2000-fold dilution.
Pipette up and down for several times and load the mixture into a 384 well plate.
Prepare qPCR master mixture according to specified protocol.
Centrifuge briefly to bring the sample to the bottom of the tube.
Perform qPCR program at 98°C for 10 minutes.
Cycle the qPCR program at 98°C for 15 seconds and then 60°C for 30 seconds, followed by 72°C for 30 seconds. Repeat this cycle 39 times.
Analyze qPCR data by plotting a standard curve.
Calculate the AAV8 physical titer using the plotted standard curve.
Determine the proper dilution for qPCR standard curve by pretesting.
Include a no-template control (NTC) in master mix plus water for qPCR experiments.
Perform virus dilution empirically based on construct and genome size, typically 2000-fold for pAAV_sgGOI_sg3TSG_Cre.
Use transduction assays to test infectivity of AAV8 prior to experiments.
Choose from two alternative transduction assays as per experimental needs.
Titer the AAV virus by isolating ASF from Rosa-26-LSL-Cas9-eGFP mice.
Plate 15,000 ASF per well in a 24-well plate.
Thaw one aliquot of the AAV viral stock at −80°C on ice.
Dilute AAV in complete media plus polybrene (1:1000).
Add 500 μL of virus-containing media to each well.
Remove virus-containing media after 24 hours and replace with pre-warmed complete media.
Analyze GFP expression level of infected cells using flow cytometry at 72 hours post-transfection.
Calculate the titer in transduction units (TU/mL) based on the number of cells, dilution factor, and volume used.
Thaw one aliquot of the AAV viral stock on ice.
Dilute the AAV stock according to previous qPCR results into three dilutions in recovery solution: 1.85∗109, 9.25∗109, and 3.7∗1010 viral genomes per mice in a volume of 200 μL.
Gently pipette up and down the virus several times to mix.
Weigh mice before injecting AAV intraperitoneally.
Euthanize mice seven days post injection.
Collect pancreas tissue after euthanasia.
Isolate pancreas into single cells.
Detect GFP expression in pancreatic cells by flow cytometry.
Sort transfected pancreatic cells using fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS).
Extract genomic DNA from sorted cells using QuickExtract™ DNA Extraction Solution 1.0.
Design PCR primers according to TIDE website’s instructions.
Purify PCR product from DNA gel.
Send purified PCR product for Sanger sequencing.
Load sample chromatogram into TIDE.
Calculate the percentage of indels in the sequence data.
